messages:
lucy: Quick alert — canary 10k RPS run showed a 2.1x tail latency spike on ingress compared to baseline. Looks host-side. Flame and perf samples attached. :eyes:
ajay: ugh. seen anything in kernel selection or batching heuristics?
mara: also saw higher tokenization CPU during the run, could be small-write chatty requests causing repeated tokenizer coldpaths.
lucy: exact hotspot from pprof (sample):
```
 28.3%  writev_coalesce
 14.9%  grpc::Stream::flush
 12.4%  tokenizer::fast_parse
  9.8%  kvcache::evict_if_needed
  6.2%  socket::nagle_fallback
```
ajay: writev_coalesce that high suggests we aren't bundling small chunks at the host proxy. Was the http2->grpc bridge involved on that canary?
lucy: yes - test path was http1 client -> gateway -> host-proxy -> runtime (gRPC). The gateway flusher configured to low-latency (flush_every=1).
jorge: did the batcher change recently? we moved dynamic_batch_hint to prefer smaller batches for chatty sessions last week. Could be reducing kernel-friendly sequence lengths and toggling kernel selection to scalar fallback.
han: i ran a micro-bench: when average seq_len < 32 kernel selector picks scalar kernels which are 20-30% slower per-token on our AVX machines. If dynamic batching pushes more tiny seqs, we lose throughput and increase CPU per-request.
mara: kvcache evictions correlate with spike windows — hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 68% under the same load. suspect increased fragmentation from many small requests bypassing prefix cache grouping.
lucy: good summary. Hypotheses: 1) flusher frequency causing many tiny writes -> writev/flush overhead, 2) batching heuristics increasing tiny sequences -> worse kernel selection, 3) small writes lead to fragmented KV cache keys and more evictions.
ajay: can we repro with a controlled config matrix? change flush_every=5, set batch_hint=min(64, tokens), and run with kvcache grouping on session id?
ci-bot: triggered perf-job #perf/175451 — matrix: flush={1,5,20}, batch_hint={auto,64}, kvcache_group={off,on}. Will post artifacts.
jorge: also add tcp_nodelay toggle to matrix — if socket coalescing interacts with grpc flush path it might reduce writev count.
han: quick mitigation I can try on canary: enable small-write coalescer in host-proxy (buffer up to 4ms or 8KB) and pin kernel selector to prefer vector kernels for seq_len threshold 24. Want me to push?
lucy: yes please. Start with coalescer=4ms + kernel_threshold=24. Run the same 10k RPS profile.
mara: capture pprof + kvcache metrics and the runtime kernel decision logs (we added trace points last month). Also grab percentage of requests hitting scalar vs vector kernels.
ajay: if that helps, we can longer-term make kernel selector aware of batching_hint so it doesn't flip to scalar when batches are expected to join.
lucy: results from quick patch on canary (coalescer=4ms + kernel_threshold=24): tail latency down ~35%, writev samples dropped ~3x, kvcache hit ratio recovered to ~89%.
jorge: nice. Any regressions on p99 CPU or memory?
han: no memory bump. CPU per-host slightly lower overall because vector kernels win at throughput; p99 CPU consumption still within SLA.
mara: next steps: prod canary rollout with coalescer and threshold, longer soak test, then follow-up: revisit batching policy and kvcache key grouping to avoid fragmentation.
lucy: I'll open a small RFC for batching->kernel co-design and kvcache grouping heuristics. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
ajay: add a note to the console alerts so future canaries flag sudden writev flame percents.
ci-bot: perf-job #perf/175451 completed: artifacts -> https://ci.internal/perf/175451/artifacts
lucy: attaching logs and pprof links in the RFC. Filing postmortem if any relapse after rollout.
notes: small thread: config repro, quick mitigation verified on canary - followups: RFC for batching/kernels and kvcache grouping
